source.title: Gree Mini Split (GMS) BACnet Converter User Manual

model: GMS BACnet Converter (GMS GW) - M/W/P/X series with DWUNI
applies_to: Gree M, W, P and X series split indoor units with a DWUNI wired controller connected to a GMS GW 1 or GMS GW 12.
summary: Same Gree GMS gateway as the R-series entry, but for M/W/P/X series units on a DWUNI wired controller. The common Class 0 objects are identical; the Class 1 series-specific objects use their own numbering.
notes: Instance formula: Class x 1048576 + (Line - 1) x 131072 + remote control address x 256 + object number. Common objects are Class 0, series-specific objects Class 1. This file lists line 1, address 1 (L1.001).
Each split unit needs a unique remote control address (0-63 per line), set from its wired controller; the gateway shows it as L<line>.<address>.
The manual has no read/write column; access was inferred from object type (BV/AV/MV writable, BI/AI/PIV read-only).
The gateway is made by CoolAutomation for Gree; GMS GW 1 handles one unit, GMS GW 12 up to 12 units over two RS-485 lines.
R-series units use a different Class 1 object set (see the separate GMS GW R-series entry).

integration.enable: No enable point; a unit is controllable once it has a unique remote control address on line L1 or L2. BV 'Global Lock' and the two Lock BVs stop local wired-controller changes.
setup: Device instance is set from the gateway's LCD menu (Menu > BACnet > Instance number) and takes effect after a restart.
The BAC A/B RS-485 port runs either BACnet MS/TP or Modbus RTU; choose BACnet in the 'Line 3' setting of the USB configuration tool.
BACnet/IP runs on the Ethernet port; network settings are changed with the ifconfig command in the gateway terminal.
Set each indoor unit's remote control address (0-63) on its wired controller before mapping objects.
integration.summary: Address each split unit from its DWUNI wired controller, pick BACnet/IP or MS/TP, set a unique device instance from the LCD menu, then map each unit's object block using the instance formula. Control uses the common on/off, mode, fan and setpoint objects.

minimum_points.name: Fan Speed
minimum_points.why: Low / medium / high / auto (plus extra speeds)

minimum_points.name: split unit Failure Status
minimum_points.why: Failure flag; Active_Text carries the code

gotchas: Instances are computed from line and remote control address, so re-addressing a unit moves all of its objects.
DWUNI units have a single Set Point Limits Enable (BV 12) instead of separate cooling/heating enables.
Class 1 object numbers overlap with R-series objects of different meaning; don't reuse an R-series template.

note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source). Point availability varies by firmware and options; verify against the live device.
